# Rules

## 1. Overview

Build and grow an empire. Expand your territory, grow your cities, research technologies, construct buildings, found cities, and conquer rivals.

Money is the game's only resource. Population, technologies, buildings, armies, and fleets are all bought with it.

### If you have played other 4X games

- **Armies never stand on the map.** They stay in your cities and project power outward. You never move a unit onto a tile.
- **There is no attack command.** After every player ends their turn, your siege advances automatically if your projection exceeds both the city’s defense and every other attacker’s projection.
- **Fleets are not transports.** There is no embark action. Fleets control sea tiles from coastal cities, and army routes cross controlled sea on their own.
- **City sites are fixed when the map is created.** Cities may be founded only at those sites. After every player ends their turn, the right to settle is awarded to the sole player whose projection there exceeds every rival’s.
- **Everyone plays at once.** All players act during the same turn. You see each rival’s fleets and newly claimed land as they were at the start of the turn; all other visible information is current. When the turn ends you are shown what changed hands.

You may undo anything until you end your turn. Ending your turn is final.

Victory is checked after every player ends their turn. If only one empire remains, it wins. If any empire has at least 100 victory points (VP), the empire with the most VP wins. Ties are broken by money.

## 2. The World

The map consists of hexagonal tiles grouped into provinces. Each province contains either one city or an empty site where a city may be founded.

Each empire has one capital. Minor Powers are neutral factions that each hold one city.

Civilizations have no gameplay differences; your choice only biases your capital’s starting location.

An unclaimed tile belongs to nobody. The owner of a province’s city may claim tiles in that province. Once claimed, a tile remains attached to that city and changes owner with it.

## 3. One Turn

Every player plays the same turn at the same time.

While the turn is open:

1. **Everyone acts at once.** You act against the other players, and they act against you, during the same turn. Your own actions affect your empire immediately.
2. **You may undo actions.** Undo is unlimited until you end your turn.
3. **You end your turn.** Ending your turn is irreversible, and you take no further action this turn.
4. **You receive income.** Income is paid at that moment, and every other effect triggered by ending your turn is applied then. Your claim and growth allowances reset.

After every player ends their turn:

1. All sieges are evaluated from the same pre-capture position.
2. Completed sieges capture their cities.
3. Settle rights for the next turn are determined.
4. Minor Powers act.
5. Victory is checked.

Nothing contested is settled until then: an army you buy still counts against a rival who ended their turn before you. Then the next turn begins, and you are shown what changed hands.

## 4. Money, Cities, and Land

### Income

At the end of your turn, you receive:

> $3 + the income of every city in your empire

Trade can provide additional income.

### City Growth

A city gains levels by earning experience. Its level determines its income. Population and land development are the main sources of experience.

| Level | Total experience required | Income | VP per turn |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0 | $1 | — |
| 2 | 3 | $2 | — |
| 3 | 10 | $4 | — |
| 4 | 25 | $7 | — |
| 5 | 50 | $11 | — |
| 6 | 100 | $13 | 1 |
| 7+ | 150, then +50 per level | $13 | 1 |

The first city in your empire to reach level 3 awards 2 VP. The first to reach level 5 awards 5 VP.

Every level gained beyond level 6 awards 5 VP. Further levels do not increase income.

### Population

Adding population costs:

> $2 + $2 for each population already in the city

The city gains 1 population and 2 experience.

Your empire may grow once per turn.

### Claiming and Clearing Land

Claiming brings a tile into your empire. Clearing improves certain types of claimed terrain for a one-time benefit.

Your empire may claim or clear a total of two tiles per turn. Each claim or clear counts toward this shared limit.

A tile may be claimed if it:

- Belongs to one of your cities’ provinces
- Is no more than 3 tiles from that city

The claim costs an amount of money equal to its hex distance from the city.

Claiming land grants experience as follows:

- Plains: 1 experience immediately
- Forest, Steppe, or Marsh: no experience until cleared
- Any other terrain: no experience

Only claimed land may be cleared.

| Terrain | Required technology | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forest | Iron Working | Gain $2 and 1 experience; becomes Plains |
| Steppe | Steel | Pay $1 and gain 2 experience |
| Marsh | Drainage | Pay $2 and gain 2 experience |

A tile may be cleared only once.

## 5. Technologies

Researching a technology costs money. Its effects and unlocked content apply immediately.

If a technology has several prerequisites, any one is sufficient.

Every researched technology awards 2 VP.

Cities may reduce technology prices:

- Level 3 or 4: 10% discount
- Level 5 or higher: 20% discount

Apply the largest discount available from a single city. Round the final price down.

## 6. Buildings

A building is constructed in one city. It requires money and one available building slot.

A city has:

> Population ÷ 2 building slots, rounded down

Upgrading a building replaces the previous building and uses the same slot. The previous building’s effects end.

Ordinary buildings have no empire-wide limit. Unique buildings are limited across your entire empire; technologies determine how many of each your empire may hold.

Some buildings grant a one-time bonus when their city first reaches or passes a specified population or level. The building must already exist when the threshold is crossed.

## 7. Armies and Land Projection

### Armies

Armies remain stationed in cities. They do not occupy or move through individual tiles.

Buying one army costs:

> $3 + $2 for each army already in your empire

A city may hold:

> 1 + population ÷ 3, rounded down, plus building effects

Army transfers and military projection use the valid route with the lowest total decay.

### Land Route Decay

| Terrain entered | Base decay |
| --- | --- |
| Plains | 4 |
| Steppe or Hills | 8 |
| Forest | 10 |
| Desert, Marsh, Tundra, or Jungle | 16 |

Multiply the base decay according to the tile’s owner:

| Tile | Multiplier |
| --- | --- |
| Your claimed tile | ×1 |
| Unclaimed tile | ×2 |
| Another empire’s or Minor Power’s tile | ×4 |

A river halves the tile’s decay.

Mountains and waters cannot be crossed.

### Army Transfers

You may transfer an army directly between two of your cities along any valid route, regardless of its total decay.

The transfer costs:

> $1 per 20 route decay, rounded up

### Military Projection

Each army has base strength 2. Technologies and buildings may increase it.

Armies project only along routes with total decay of 50 or less. Within that range:

> Remaining projection = 100% − route decay

Each city projects:

> Armies × army strength × remaining projection

Apply any effect that explicitly modifies this projection. Add together the projection from all your cities to determine your total projection at a destination.

## 8. Fleets, Sea, and Trade

### Fleets

Fleets remain stationed in coastal cities.

Buying one fleet costs:

> $4 + $3 for each fleet already in your empire

A city may hold:

> 1 + population ÷ 5, rounded down, plus building effects

Each fleet has base strength 2. Technologies and buildings may increase it.

### Fleet Projection

Fleet projection travels only through Sea. Each Sea tile adds 8 decay.

> Remaining projection = 100% − fleet decay, to a minimum of 0%

Each coastal city projects:

> Fleets × fleet strength × remaining projection

Apply any effect that explicitly modifies this projection. Add projection from all your coastal cities.

Fleet projection is compared only with fleet projection from other players. Fleets cannot besiege cities.

### Fleet Bridges

You may use a Sea tile as a bridge if your fleet projection there:

- Is at least 1
- Is at least as high as every other player’s projection

Every player tied for the highest qualifying projection may use that tile as a bridge.

Armies may cross Sea through these bridges. Each bridged Sea tile adds 2 army route decay. Ownership multipliers do not apply to Sea.

### Fleet Movement

Fleets move directly between coastal cities. Their route may pass through Sea and your claimed land.

Fleet route decay is:

- 8 decay per Sea tile
- 32 decay per land tile

Use the valid route with the lowest total decay.

Movement costs:

> $1 per 20 fleet-route decay, rounded up

### Trade

After researching Trade, each non-capital city connected to your capital provides $1 additional income per turn.

A connection may pass through:

- Your cities
- Your claimed land
- Sea tiles you may use as fleet bridges

## 9. Sieges and Capture

Sieges happen automatically. You do not declare an attack or assign armies to a target.

After every player ends their turn, your siege against a city advances if your projection there is:

- Greater than the city’s defense
- Greater than every other attacker’s projection

A player city’s defense is:

> 2 per level + its owner’s projection there

A Minor Power’s defense is:

> 2 per level + 2 per defender

A siege has three stages, and a technology can reduce that. Meeting both conditions advances your siege one stage. If either condition is not met, your siege loses one stage of progress. Siege progress cannot fall below zero.

Completing the last stage captures the city.

A captured city retains its level, experience, population, claimed land, and ordinary buildings. Its units are removed and its unique buildings are destroyed.

Capturing a capital awards 6 VP and eliminates its owner. Each remaining city of the defeated empire becomes a separate Minor Power.

## 10. Founding Cities

Places where cities may be founded are fixed when the map is created.

After every player ends their turn, the sole player whose projection at an empty site exceeds every rival’s gains the right to found a city there during the next turn.

Each city you hold adds 1 to that projection, even if it holds no armies, and this contribution is reduced by route decay as normal. An uncontested site within reach therefore automatically grants settle rights without requiring armies to be stationed there in advance.

To found a city:

1. Select one of your cities as the source city.
2. Choose the Settle action.

The source city loses 2 armies, and you pay $2 per 20 route decay, rounded up. A new level-1 city with population 1 is founded at the site.

## 11. Minor Powers

Minor Powers are neutral factions.

They do not:

- Research technologies
- Project military power
- Hold two or more cities
- Construct or hold buildings

After every player ends their turn, each Minor Power may claim land, gain population, or add defenders.

Minor Powers have three temperaments:

- **Prosperous:** more likely to gain experience and increase its level, which makes it steadily harder to capture
- **Fortified:** more likely to add defenders, and the hardest to capture
- **Dormant:** less likely to act, and the easiest to capture

### Alarm

Beginning on turn 4, when a Minor Power is under siege or falls, other Minor Powers within 7 tiles become alarmed. Each alarmed Minor Power gains additional chances to add defenders.

## 12. Victory Points

Victory points (VP) are an abstract measure of your empire’s achievements. You gain VP from:

- Each technology researched: +2 VP
- Certain buildings: as stated in their effects
- Your empire’s first city to reach level 3: +2 VP
- Your empire’s first city to reach level 5: +5 VP
- Each level 6 or higher city: +1 VP per turn
- Each level gained beyond level 6: +5 VP

Reaching 10, 30, and 60 VP unlocks one permanent policy choice at each threshold. You must resolve a pending policy before taking another action.

## 13. Victory

Victory is checked after every player ends their turn.

If only one empire remains, it wins.

If any empire has at least 100 VP, the empire with the most VP wins.

Ties are broken by money.

# Controls

## Action panel

- Select a map tile, a city, Research, or Macros to change what appears in Actions.
- Macros let you perform multiple actions with a single button.

## Map overlays

- **Reach:** Shows how far an Army can project power from the selected city.
- **Projection:** Colors each tile by the strongest Army projection.

# Player interface and diagnostics

This appendix records player-visible behavior that is not fully described by the Rules, Codex, or Controls. It is not a second rules source.

- **Contextual actions:** Select one of your cities to see that city's actions. Select eligible land in a province whose city you own to see its Claim or Clear action. Select an empty city site to see Settle actions for that site, or a rival city to see an available siege macro for that target. Selecting a city name also selects and centers that city.
- **Research and Macros:** The number beside `Research` or `Macros` is the number of actions that can be executed now; a count of zero can still be opened. Macros are currently legal multi-action convenience bundles, not strategic recommendations, and their stable order is not a strength ranking.
- **Visible, disabled, and absent actions:** An otherwise available but unaffordable action stays visible with its price and no redundant insufficient-money reason. Other blockers may keep a row disabled and replace its detail with a reason. Exhausted claim/clear and growth groups are replaced by status text. A full building group is replaced only when no available upgrade can reuse its base building's slot. Content not yet unlocked by technology can be absent.
- **Temporary action gates:** A pending policy choice replaces ordinary actions and gates `Research`, `Macros`, and `End turn` until it is resolved. During the end-of-turn reveal, ordinary actions are replaced by a reveal status. A selection with no applicable action shows guidance to select an actionable target.
- **City diagnostics:** The city panel (available only for your own cities) shows level and experience progress, population, income, building slots used and total, Army count and limit, Fleet count and limit for coastal cities, built buildings, and siege pressure when present. A Grow row shows its price and the population and experience that action will add after current policy and building effects.
- **Direction and projection diagnostics:** Move is listed on the selected source city and names the destination. A city-side Settle row names its target; a site-side Settle row also names its source city. With map overlays off, selecting an occupied city or Minor Power shows its Defense breakdown and any attacker or tied attackers with the strongest projection. In Projection, selecting a tile shows every empire's Army projection there, or Fleet projection on water.

# Introduction Map

- The first game defaults to a fixed two-player map.
- The human capital starts inland at level 1 with population 2, $10, no Armies, and no claimed land. Within its province and claim range are five Plains tiles, including two adjacent to the capital, and seven Forest tiles.
- A nearby empty inland city site is within the capital's initial settlement reach.
- The nearby Minor Power is Dormant and coastal, starting at level 1 with no defenders. Its initial defense is 2; the land route from the capital retains 52% of Army strength.
- The human capital and nearby empty site are inland. The nearby Minor Power's city provides coastal access toward the next island's empty site and Prosperous Minor Power.
- Further sea connections lead toward the rival's inland capital and a Fortified Minor Power. There is only one rival empire.
